themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 45 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 10.9 per week, a 314% spike suggesting rapid pavement or infrastructure degradation across East Flatbush that warrants immediate investigation into cause and scope.
evidence: 45 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (314% increase)
Z-score of 6.55 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
Spike appears concentrated in current week with no prior warning signals in recent data
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify whether deterioration is concentrated in specific blocks or corridors (pothole clusters, flooding zones, subsidence)
Interview NYC DOT about recent weather events, utility work, or infrastructure maintenance schedules that may have triggered damage

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Emergencies
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints exploded to 4 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week, a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72) signaling potential widespread electrical hazards, fires, or grid stress requiring urgent verification and resident safety assessment.
evidence: 4 electrical complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% increase)
Highest z-score in dataset (11.72) indicates most extreme statistical anomaly
Pattern suggests acute trigger rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Contact FDNY and Con Edison to cross-reference electrical emergencies, power outages, or equipment failures reported in East Flatbush this week
Interview residents and building managers in affected areas about blackouts, sparking outlets, burnt breakers, or fire alarm triggers

themes_detail.label: Food Establishment Health Violations
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK versus a 1.8 weekly average, a 243% spike suggesting potential foodborne illness risks, sanitation failures, or enforcement action that could affect community health.
evidence: 6 food establishment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (243% increase)
Z-score of 4.39 indicates significant statistical deviation
Spike is recent with no sustained prior elevated baseline
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with NYC Health Department inspection records to identify specific establishments cited THIS WEEK and violation types (pests, temperature abuse, hygiene)
Determine whether spike reflects new enforcement actions, a single outbreak, or multiple independent violations across different venues

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage and Decline Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Combined tree complaints (damaged and dead/dying trees) reached 15 LAST WEEK versus a 2.8 weekly average, a 435% combined spike suggesting environmental stress, storm damage, or disease affecting the district's canopy.
evidence: Damaged trees: 11 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly average (363% increase, z-score: 4.32)
Dead/dying trees: 4 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% increase, z-score: 7.49)
Combined 15 tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. ~3.2 baseline suggests localized environmental event or infrastructure conflict
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent storm, utility work (power line trimming, water main breaks), pests (spotted lanternfly, emerald ash borer), or disease outbreak caused spike
Interview NYC Parks about tree inventory health in East Flatbush and whether canopy loss correlates with heat vulnerability (HEAT/HOT WATER leads district at 4,836 complaints over 90 days)

themes_detail.label: Waste Management System Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Residential and commercial disposal complaints combined for 11 LAST WEEK versus a 3.0 baseline average, a 267% combined spike suggesting sanitation collection failures, illegal dumping, or contamination that may affect public health.
evidence: Residential disposal: 8 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly average (191% increase, z-score: 4.38)
Commercial disposal: 3 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score: 4.16)
Combined spike suggests systemic collection or management issue rather than isolated complaints
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation to determine whether LAST WEEK included missed pickups, route changes, or vehicle breakdowns in East Flatbush
Investigate whether illegal dumping complaints cluster in specific neighborhoods and whether enforcement action is needed
